title: Errors, Known Issues and Escalation
brief: Given 8 symptom reports, classify each one: curation, platform bug, performance,
expected variation, or governance. Name the evidence you would capture for each.
Write the escalation note for the two that are genuine platform bugs.
Knowing which problems were never yours to fix is most of this job. An escalation that
arrives without a reproduction, a workspace id and a timestamp goes to the back of a
review: Exactly two are classified as platform bugs, and they are the right two.
At least one is correctly called expected variation rather than a defect.
Each escalation note carries a reproduction, a timestamp, and what was already ruled out.
No item is escalated that the author could have fixed in curation.

inputs.title: Eight symptom reports, as they were raised
rows: Classify: curation · platform bug · performance · expected variation · governance
1. "Genie gave me a different number this morning than yesterday for the same
question. Nothing changed in the data."
2. "Every question takes 40 seconds. The warehouse is a 2X-Large and idle."
3. "It says 'no results' for Northeast but there are definitely clients there."
4. "The answer cites a column that does not exist in the table I can see."
5. "I asked for client emails and got a column of asterisks."
6. "The SQL it wrote is valid but it returned an error about statement timeout
after about 90 seconds. It reproduces every time on the same question."
7. "My colleague gets a number and I get an empty table for the same question."
8. "The conversation stopped responding after roughly ten minutes and the
answer never appeared, but it still shows on our usage."
Exactly two are platform bugs. Write the escalation note for those two: a
reproduction, a timestamp, the workspace id, and what you already ruled out.
At least one is expected variation and should be closed, not escalated.
